errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the units alone, with no computation: units offered as optional is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, units of the quantity given for its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and correct units spoken with the written answer bare is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Units omitted or assembled the wrong way round
non_conceptual_causes: the units are written on scratch work and not transferred to the answer line
the unit of the independent variable is taken from a different sentence of the stem
the part is reached at the end of the question and the answer line is filled last
errors.observed_behavior: A correct numerical rate is reported with no units, or with the units of the quantity alone, or with the numerator and denominator units exchanged.
errors.scoring_consequence: The units point is a separate point in the 2024 and 2025 table based questions and is lost outright (sg-24:2, sg-25:11); BC-ERR-99005 records the same behaviour across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the two quantities the units in the stem describe: treating the function and its derivative as the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, ignoring what the sign of the rate records is consistent with BC-MIS-04002, and a correct match with the wrong number written is consistent with the row and transfer causes.
errors.name: Amount reported where a rate was requested
non_conceptual_causes: the wrong row of the supplied table is read
the stem's phrase rate at which is skimmed
both quantities are computed and the wrong one is transferred to the answer line
errors.observed_behavior: The response supplies a value of the modelled function where the question asked for a value of its derivative, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; BC-ERR-99030 records confusion of the direction of change with the quantity itself.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which two table entries were used and what was done with them: an answer that the quotient alone is the object is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, an answer that the tabulated amounts are already the rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming both entries at once is consistent with the calculator and transfer causes.
errors.name: Difference quotient presented without the difference
non_conceptual_causes: the subtraction and division are done on the calculator and only the result is written
the two table entries are differenced mentally
the setup line is written on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is written as a single quotient or as a bare number with no visible difference of tabulated values.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 rubric states that the setup expression by itself is not sufficient for the point, which requires the answer together with a difference and a quotient using values from the table (sg-25:11).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the quantity was larger or smaller a moment later: an answer that the sign carries no information is consistent with BC-MIS-04002, an answer drawn from the amount rather than its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and a correct direction beside the unsigned written answer is consistent with the transcription and template causes.
errors.name: Sign of a rate not interpreted
non_conceptual_causes: the minus sign is dropped when the value is copied from the calculator
the stem's word decreasing is read as an instruction to report a magnitude
the interpretation sentence is written from the previous part's template
errors.observed_behavior: A negative rate is reported as a magnitude or is described as an increase.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost; BC-ERR-99030 records the same confusion of direction with quantity.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write which function the stem supplied before differentiating: treating position, velocity, and acceleration as unrelated formulas is consistent with BC-MIS-04004, treating a quantity and its rate as the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and identifying the supplied function correctly is consistent with the carry-over and habit causes.
errors.name: Differentiation performed the wrong number of times for the quantity requested
non_conceptual_causes: the function the stem supplied is not identified before differentiating
the previous part's answer is carried forward as the starting function
the derivative is taken twice out of habit from a practised example
errors.observed_behavior: Acceleration is reported where velocity was asked for, or position where velocity was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although each differentiation performed is correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether a speed can be negative and what the sign of the velocity records instead: an answer that the two are one quantity is consistent with BC-MIS-04005, an answer that acceleration alone governs speed is consistent with BC-MIS-99001, and a correct distinction beside the signed written answer is consistent with the transfer and wording causes.
errors.name: Speed reported as a signed quantity
non_conceptual_causes: the absolute value is applied on scratch work and not transferred
the velocity value is copied straight from the calculator
the words speed and velocity are used interchangeably in the answer sentence
errors.observed_behavior: A negative number is reported as the speed of the particle.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what quantity has to be negative for the particle to move in the negative direction: an answer naming the position is consistent with BC-MIS-04005, an answer that the position already carries its rate is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming the velocity correctly is consistent with the misread figure and ordering causes.
errors.name: Direction of motion read from the position rather than the velocity
non_conceptual_causes: the supplied graph is of position and is read as velocity
the sign is read from the table row above the intended one
the conclusion is written before the velocity is computed
errors.observed_behavior: The response argues the direction of travel from whether the position is positive or negative.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reasoning point is lost; the 2022 Chief Reader report records responses arguing from the wrong function in a related part (cr-22:20).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to solve the equation velocity equal to zero explicitly: an answer that the sampled values settle the interval is consistent with BC-MIS-04017, an answer that confuses the sign change with a change of speed is consistent with BC-MIS-04005, and finding the root once the equation is solved is consistent with the window and table step causes.
errors.name: Zeros of velocity found by sampling integer times
non_conceptual_causes: the equation is judged unsolvable by hand so integer inputs are tried instead
the calculator zero feature is used on a window that hides the root
the table step is one unit so a non integer root falls between rows
errors.observed_behavior: Integer times are substituted into the velocity in place of solving the equation velocity equal to zero, so a non-integer zero is missed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 Chief Reader report records this behaviour directly and links it to the loss of the two analysis points, whose mean scores were 0.04 and 0.03 (crabbc-25:20, crabbc-25:22).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to say in one sentence what the chart shows about the interval named in the prompt: an answer that the sampled signs settle it is consistent with BC-MIS-04017, an answer that restates the chart as its own reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, and a fluent sentence with none written is consistent with the timing and interval causes.
errors.name: Sign chart presented with no stated reading
non_conceptual_causes: the reading sentence is left to the end of the part and not reached
the chart is treated as sufficient because an earlier part accepted one
the chart covers an interval other than the one the prompt names
errors.observed_behavior: A number line or table of signs appears with no sentence saying what it shows about the direction of motion over the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 report records that responses failing to communicate what the chart showed over the whole interval did not earn the analysis points (crabbc-25:22, crabbc-25:23); BC-ERR-99001 records vague referents in justification across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the letters in the model stand for before any computation: an answer that borrows motion language for a non motion quantity is consistent with BC-MIS-04007, an answer that treats the descriptive units as ornament is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, and correct descriptions given orally is consistent with the copying and transfer causes.
errors.name: Quantity and independent variable not named
non_conceptual_causes: the letters are copied from the stem without their descriptions
the naming is written on the diagram and not in the response
the computation is started first because the numbers were already to hand
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes without saying which quantity is modelled or what the input variable measures.
errors.scoring_consequence: Later interpretation points become unavailable because the answer cannot be tied to the situation; BC-ERR-99033 records variables introduced without being defined.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the quantity whose rate is being described: an answer that every rate problem is a motion problem is consistent with BC-MIS-04007, an answer that the quantity and its rate are one object is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and the correct noun supplied at once is consistent with the carry-over and template causes.
errors.name: Motion vocabulary used for a non-motion quantity
non_conceptual_causes: the word velocity is carried over from the preceding motion question
the answer sentence is adapted from a motion template
the units of the rate are not consulted before the noun is chosen
errors.observed_behavior: The response calls the rate of change of a temperature, a population, or an area a velocity.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2025 scoring notes show a response calling an average value an average velocity treated as unclear communication and scored as scratch work, so the points survived in that instance (sg-25:3); the CED nonetheless directs that context vocabulary be used (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write each rate in derivative notation and mark which is unknown: an answer that differentiates against a length rather than time is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, an answer that an instantaneous value holds throughout is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and a correct marking beside the transposed written work is consistent with the notation and transcription causes.
errors.name: Given and requested rates not distinguished
non_conceptual_causes: the two rates are never written in derivative notation before the algebra begins
the rate supplied in the stem is the only number available and is reported
the roles are correct on scratch work and transposed in the copy
errors.observed_behavior: The rate supplied in the stem is reported as the answer, or the requested rate is treated as known.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; BC-ERR-99033 records variables introduced without being defined as a related communication failure.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to draw the configuration and label every length before writing a formula: an answer assembled from the rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, an answer that differentiates against a length is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, and a correct formula once the diagram is drawn is consistent with the recall and shape causes.
errors.name: Relating equation wrong or absent
non_conceptual_causes: the geometric formula is misremembered, for instance a cone's volume without the factor one third
no diagram is drawn so the configuration is guessed
the formula is taken from a similar problem with a different shape
errors.observed_behavior: No equation ties the quantities together, or the formula used does not describe the configuration.
errors.scoring_consequence: Nothing downstream can be earned; BC-ERR-99011 records integrands chosen from the wrong area or volume family as the analogous failure in Unit 8.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what variable the requested rate is taken with respect to, before differentiating: an answer naming a length is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, an answer that the two derivative variables give the same object is consistent with BC-MIS-99005, and naming time correctly beside the wrong written derivative is consistent with the ordering and habit causes.
errors.name: Differentiation carried out with respect to the wrong variable
non_conceptual_causes: the differentiation is carried out against the variable that appears first
the chain rule factor with respect to time is written and not carried to the next line
the habit of differentiating with respect to x is carried from the implicit differentiation topic
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation is differentiated with respect to a length or with respect to x, and the response stops there rather than continuing through the chain rule to a rate with respect to time.
errors.scoring_consequence: The Chief Reader report for 2024 records that responses differentiating with respect to x needed to continue through the chain rule and that many provided no work beyond that step (cr-24:18); BC-ERR-99013 records the same family across years.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the two factors of the term before differentiating it: an answer naming one symbol is consistent with BC-MIS-04009, an answer that treats one factor as fixed is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and naming both factors with one term still missing on paper is consistent with the substitution and transcription causes.
errors.name: Product rule omitted inside a differentiation with respect to time
non_conceptual_causes: the short term is read as one symbol
one factor is replaced by its instantaneous value before the differentiation
the product rule is applied and one of its two terms is dropped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: A term that multiplies two varying quantities is differentiated as though one of them were constant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The completely correct differentiation point is lost; BC-ERR-99013 names the missing product rule explicitly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many unknown rates the differentiated equation contains: an answer assembled from the supplied rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, an answer that an instantaneous value holds throughout is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, and counting two at once is consistent with the unwritten proportion and timing causes.
errors.name: Extra varying quantity never eliminated
non_conceptual_causes: the similar triangles proportion is seen and never written
the second dimension is assumed constant with no sentence saying so
the differentiated equation is left with two unknown rates and the part ends
errors.observed_behavior: The relating equation keeps two varying dimensions that the supplied rates cannot support, and the differentiation produces an equation with two unknown rates.
errors.scoring_consequence: The requested rate cannot be isolated, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the stated numbers would still be true one second later: an answer that all of them would is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer that treats the product of two varying quantities as one symbol is consistent with BC-MIS-04009, and a correct answer with the early substitution still on paper is consistent with the simplification and setup causes.
errors.name: Instantaneous values substituted before differentiating
non_conceptual_causes: the substitution is made to simplify the algebra before differentiating
the number is read from the stem as a fixed feature of the configuration
the value and the rate of the same quantity are confused in the setup table
errors.observed_behavior: A dimension that varies with time is replaced by its value at the instant before the equation is differentiated, so its rate never appears.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiated equation is wrong and the answer follows it; the CED sample activity asks students to mark which given information always applies and which applies only at an instant, which is the distinction at stake (ced:86).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to name the single unknown in the equation and isolate it: an answer that the instantaneous relation is already the result is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer that differentiates against the wrong variable is consistent with BC-MIS-04008, and a prompt isolation is consistent with the timing and transfer causes.
errors.name: Requested rate never isolated
non_conceptual_causes: the algebra is left to the end of the question and not returned to
the differentiated equation is taken as the answer because it contains the requested symbol
the isolation is carried out on scratch work and not transferred
errors.observed_behavior: The differentiated equation is correct and the response stops without solving for the unknown rate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The final scoring point is lost although the differentiation points may be earned (cr-24:18).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which quantities the differentiated equation needs and which of them the stem supplies: an answer that the instant's stated values are all there is is consistent with BC-MIS-04011, an answer built from the rates alone is consistent with BC-MIS-04010, and spotting the gap on request is consistent with the auxiliary computation and one line causes.
errors.name: Missing instantaneous value not computed
non_conceptual_causes: the quantity is assumed given because the stem supplies its rate
the auxiliary computation from the relating equation is never attempted
the substitution is done in one line so the omission is not noticed
errors.observed_behavior: A quantity needed for the substitution is absent from the stem and the response substitutes nothing in its place or invents a value.
errors.scoring_consequence: The substitution is incomplete and the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to check that the point satisfies the line they wrote: an answer that the tangent line is the function near the point is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that treats the equals sign as punctuation between steps is consistent with BC-MIS-99011, and a correction on substitution is consistent with the transposition and recall causes.
errors.name: Tangent line written with the point and the slope exchanged
non_conceptual_causes: the point coordinates are transposed when copied
the slope from the previous part is substituted into a coordinate slot
the point slope form is written from memory with the terms in the wrong places
errors.observed_behavior: The point-slope form is assembled incorrectly, so the coordinates appear where the slope belongs or the line does not pass through the point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost; the 2025 report records multiple sign and parenthesis errors arising while isolating the dependent variable, which was not required (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which input the question asks about and which the tangent line was built at: an answer that the line and the function agree near the point is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that a value and a rate are the same information is consistent with BC-MIS-04001, and naming the two inputs correctly is consistent with the misreading and skipped step causes.
errors.name: Tangent line evaluated at the point of tangency
non_conceptual_causes: the nearby input in the stem is misread
the tangent line is written and the substitution step is skipped
the function value already computed is reported because it is on the page
errors.observed_behavior: The approximation is produced by substituting the point of tangency rather than the nearby input, so the function value at the known point is returned.
errors.scoring_consequence: The approximation point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what feature of the supplied representation makes the concavity claim true: an answer that concavity has no bearing on the approximation is consistent with BC-MIS-07010, an answer that the symbols alone complete the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05022, and naming the feature at once is consistent with the transfer and carry-over causes.
errors.name: Concavity asserted without reference to the given representation
non_conceptual_causes: the connection is made on the supplied figure and never written
the sign of the second derivative is taken from an earlier part and reused
the justification is written at the end of the part in the shortest form to hand
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the second derivative has a sign without connecting that claim to the graph, table, or formula supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; BC-ERR-99001 records vague referents in justifications and the 2023 report records reasons not connected to the given graph (cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which point the tangent line touches before the substitution is made: an answer that the line stands in for the function anywhere is consistent with BC-MIS-04012, an answer that a single coordinate names the point is consistent with BC-MIS-05032, and naming the correct point at once is consistent with the row and reuse causes.
errors.name: Supplied derivative evaluated at the wrong point
non_conceptual_causes: the coordinates are read from the wrong row of the table
the point from an earlier part of the question is reused
only one coordinate is substituted into an expression needing both
errors.observed_behavior: An expression for the derivative involving both coordinates is evaluated at coordinates other than the point of tangency.
errors.scoring_consequence: The slope point is lost, though the approximation point may still be earned on the incorrect slope (crabbc-25:25).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the numerator limit and the denominator limit as two separate statements: an answer that the form is itself a value is consistent with BC-MIS-04014, an answer that infinity is available for arithmetic is consistent with BC-MIS-99008, and separating the two limits on request is consistent with the shorthand and equals sign causes.
errors.name: Quotient written explicitly equal to an indeterminate form
non_conceptual_causes: the shorthand is carried over from scratch work
the two limits are evaluated mentally and only the quotient is written
the equals sign is used to link the steps rather than to assert equality
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes the limit of the quotient equal to zero over zero rather than presenting the two limits separately.
errors.scoring_consequence: The 2023 rubric states that a response presenting a limit explicitly equal to zero over zero does not earn the first point, and the Chief Reader report names this arithmetic with infinity (sg-23:14, cr-23:15).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would have to be true for the rule to be usable here: an answer that it serves any awkward limit is consistent with BC-MIS-04015, an answer that the indeterminate form is a number is consistent with BC-MIS-04014, and stating the condition correctly with none written is consistent with the mental check and timing causes.
errors.name: Rule applied with no verification of the form
non_conceptual_causes: the verification is done mentally and never written
the rule is applied because the expression is a quotient
the verification sentence is cut when the part is written at speed
errors.observed_behavior: The derivatives of numerator and denominator are taken with no statement that the limit was indeterminate.
errors.scoring_consequence: The hypothesis point is lost; the CED unit overview states that students must show that the rule applies, and BC-ERR-99008 records unverified hypotheses across years (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the two derivatives on separate lines before forming the quotient: an answer that the whole quotient is differentiated is consistent with BC-MIS-04016, an answer that the rule applies to any awkward limit is consistent with BC-MIS-04015, and a correct separation on request is consistent with the one line and recency causes.
errors.name: Quotient rule applied in place of separate derivatives
non_conceptual_causes: the two rules are confused because both concern quotients
the derivative is taken in one line so the two pieces are never separated
the quotient rule is the rule most recently practised
errors.observed_behavior: The derivative of the whole quotient is taken rather than the quotient of the two derivatives.
errors.scoring_consequence: The application point is lost; the CED unit overview emphasises that the conclusion features the ratio of the derivatives rather than the derivative of the ratio (ced:84).

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to write the derivative of each piece of the numerator separately: an answer that differentiates the quotient as a whole is consistent with BC-MIS-04016, an answer that applies the rule without checking the form is consistent with BC-MIS-04015, and correct pieces beside the wrong written limit is consistent with the row and chain rule causes.
errors.name: Derivative of an unknown function in the numerator taken incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the supplied value of the derivative is read from the wrong row
the chain rule factor inside the numerator is dropped
the numerator's two pieces are differentiated as a product
errors.observed_behavior: The numerator contains a function known only through supplied properties and its derivative is mishandled, so the resulting limit is wrong.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although the hypothesis and application points may be earned; the 2023 report records incorrect derivatives of the numerator or denominator as the common failure after a correct application (cr-23:15).
